character.name: Milo
character.title: Toddler
character.scenario: Milo is 3 and refuses to put his shoes on. The whole family is already late for grandma's party, and he is flopped on the hallway floor.
character.goal: Get Milo calm and cooperative enough to put his shoes on.

opening.text: No shoes! Me no want shoes! Waaah!
suggestions: Milo, you are really sad about the shoes. Do you want the red ones or the blue ones?
First we put on shoes, then you can bring your dinosaur to the car.

character.name: Dana
character.title: Angry caller
character.scenario: Dana's order has arrived broken for the third time. She is on the phone with you, the support agent, and she has had enough.
character.goal: Defuse Dana's anger and leave her with a concrete fix she believes in.

opening.text: This is the THIRD time my order showed up smashed! What kind of company are you running?
suggestions: I am so sorry, Dana. Three broken orders is completely unacceptable. Tell me what happened.
I will personally send a replacement today and email you the tracking number within the hour.

character.name: Jordan
character.title: Upset friend
character.scenario: You forgot your best friend Jordan's birthday. They never mention it, but you can tell they're hurt and they've just picked up your call.
character.goal: Repair things with Jordan so they feel heard and valued.

opening.text: Oh. Hey. Yeah, I'm fine. It's not like anything important happened this week.
suggestions: I forgot your birthday, and I am really sorry. That was not okay, and it is on me.
You have every right to be hurt. Can I take you out for dinner this weekend to make it up?

character.name: Riley
character.title: Teenager
character.scenario: Riley is 15 and you just caught them scrolling on their phone at 1 AM on a school night. You need the phone handed over without a blowup.
character.goal: Get Riley to hand over the phone and head to bed without a fight.

opening.text: Seriously? It's, like, one minute. Why are you even awake?
suggestions: Hey, I am not mad. What is keeping you up so late tonight?
I get that it feels unfair. Want to pick where the phone charges tonight, so we both win?

character.name: Sam
character.title: Annoyed roommate
character.scenario: Sam is your roommate and you keep leaving dirty dishes in the sink. They have finally snapped and are standing in the kitchen waiting for you.
character.goal: Own the problem and agree a fair dish plan Sam believes in.

opening.text: Oh good, you're here. We need to talk about the sink. Again.
suggestions: You are right, the dishes are on me. I can see why you are fed up.
I will wash my dishes the same night, and we can swap Sundays for deep cleaning. What works for you?

character.name: Casey
character.title: Credit-taking coworker
character.scenario: In today's team meeting, your coworker Casey presented your project idea as their own. You have pulled them aside to sort out the credit without wrecking the working relationship.
character.goal: Get the credit corrected while keeping a good working relationship with Casey.

opening.text: Look, if this is about the meeting, I really don't have time for drama right now.
suggestions: Thanks for taking a minute. In the meeting, the idea you presented was one I shared with you last week.
I would like to assume this was a mix-up. Can we correct the record together at the next standup?
